topic: Dashamsha D10 done properly — lagna, 10th lord and Amatyakaraka together (DD deep-dive reel, English, 2026-09-01 pm)

slides.sub: The career chart. Almost always read backwards.

slides.body:
A varga is a divisional chart: you cut each sign into equal parts and map every part onto a full sign, producing a second chart from the same birth data.

The Dashamsha (D10) cuts each 30° sign into ten parts of 3° each. It is the varga classical texts assign to karma — profession, position, and public standing.

Take a planet's degree within its sign and divide by 3 to get which of the ten parts it falls in.

From an odd sign, count the parts from that same sign onward. From an even sign, count from the 9th from it. That single odd/even rule is where most hand-drawn D10s go wrong — and a wrong D10 reads convincingly, which is worse than an obviously broken one.

A varga has no independent life. It magnifies what the birth chart already says — it does not overrule it.

If the 10th house in D1 is weak, a glowing D10 does not cancel that. It describes the texture and the quality of what the D1 promises. Reading D10 before D1 is the single commonest error in career readings.

points: D10 lagna and its lord — the working self, how you show up professionally
The 10th lord of D1, then where it sits in the D10
Amatyakaraka — the Jaimini chara karaka at the second-highest degree, the career significator
Agreement across all three is the signal. One of the three alone is noise.
10th from the D10 Moon — the same question asked from the mind
Dignity in the D10 — exaltation and debilitation still apply inside a varga
Ashtakavarga — the benefic-point scoring system; count bindus on the D1 10th
Dasha — the planetary period system; a D10 with no running dasha gives no timing

slides.body:
It will not name a job title. Classical texts describe karma in categories — teaching, trade, service, craft, authority — not in modern job descriptions, and stretching them into one is invention, not tradition.

It also guarantees nothing. A strong D10 describes capacity and a likely season. The work still has to be done.

Then check your D1 10th lord. Do the two agree?

Comment what you find, and save this reel — the odd/even rule on slide 3 is the part people get wrong.
